$comment: Does a tajweed annotation land inside one print word? `docs/design/word-indexing.md` ⑤ asked exactly this and predicted the answer would be 'a third text' — a Tanzil segmentation this repo does not hold and has a standing rule against holding. It measured otherwise. The tajweed offsets are codepoint positions in each ayah's Tanzil Uthmani text, which cannot be read here, so it is reconstructed from the print's own per-word `data-hafs` — the string `build-words.mjs` reads and drops on purpose. Nothing is vendored and nothing ships from this but numbers. Regenerate with `pnpm probe:tajweed-words --write` (add `--fetch` on a machine whose `.cache/words/` is empty).
reads: packages/etl/data/pages/ligature-svg.probe.json — the print pin lives there and is not restated here; packages/etl/data/tajweed/tajweed.hafs.uthmani-pause-sajdah.json, whose own provenance is PROVENANCE.md beside this file.
$method: Fold the print's words into one string per ayah and ask, for every annotation, how many print words its [start, end) touches. SEVEN corrections make the fold agree with Tanzil, in two kinds, and each was earned by a run that failed without it. STRUCTURAL — how the words are joined: (1) the tajweed source prefixes the BASMALA to ayah 1 of every surah but al-Fatiha and at-Tawba — without it 326 annotations run past the end of their own ayah, with it 0; (2) the print SPLITS THE CONJUNCTION WAW that Tanzil keeps joined, and flags the split itself as `data-waw-alatf="true"`, so a flagged word is glued to its successor with no space; (3) the print NUMBERS PAUSE MARKS AS WORDS and the Tanzil text carries none of them, so they are dropped from the string — the evidence was a delta histogram clustered on EVEN values decaying monotonically (0 → 63.4%, +2 → 21.0%, +4 → 7.5%, +6 → 2.4%), the signature of one repeated two-codepoint insertion (a mark plus its space) rather than a scrambled text. Those three took the alignment from 63.40% to 97.03%. ORTHOGRAPHIC — how a single grapheme is spelled, found by bracketing each residual ayah between its last correct oracle annotation and its first wrong one and reading what lies between: (4) the print writes a small high mark on a TATWEEL CARRIER, «ـۧ» and «ـۨ», where the offsets' text writes the mark alone (97.03% → 97.56%); (5) «أٓ» is two codepoints here and three there (→ 98.49%); (6) the print carries a SMALL HIGH MADDA «ۤ» the offsets' text does not, clustering on the sajdah ayahs this edition is named for (→ 99.64%); (7) likewise a HAMZA BELOW «ٕ» on a seat (→ 99.81%). Correction 4 is deliberately narrow: generalised to every tatweel it scores 94.48%, WORSE than no correction at all, which is the evidence for its narrowness. The fold is not trusted on its own output: `hamzat_wasl` must start on ٱ and `lam_shamsiyyah` on ل, which 15,985 annotations (26.6%) can be checked against independently of any word boundary. That oracle is what decides whether the fold is right; the span arithmetic only decides what follows.
$verdict: A build change with an ELEVEN-AYAH named residual, not a third text. 99.81% of the oracle lands on the exact expected letter, and 83.31% of all 60,057 annotations fall inside ONE print word. The 16.69% that touch two words are the cross-word phonology — idghaam, ikhfa, iqlab, rules that are two-word by nature — and both boxes are paintable, so that band is a feature of tajweed rather than a defect of the fold. Exactly 1 annotation touches more than two words (12:41, idghaam_ghunnah) and 0 run past the end. The residual is 11 ayahs of 6,236 (0.18%), it is ORTHOGRAPHIC rather than structural, and every one is NAMED in `residual.named` rather than left as a rate: all 11 drift by a single constant amount, none further than ±2. Three the repo already names in a different register — 12:39 and 12:41 are two of the four print↔QAC orthographic exceptions in `lib/segmentation.mjs`, a third independent witness to the same spelling, and 15:7 is the repo's single 1→2 alignment singularity. Three more are «بَعۡدَ مَا», split by the print and joined by the offsets' text, and unlike the waw the corpus does not flag it, so it is not derivable. The rest are two bare tatweels, one small high seen, and two surah openings whose first oracle annotation is already drifted and so cannot be bracketed at all.
$blindSpots: Twelve of the eighteen rules have no characteristic letter — madd, ghunnah, qalqalah and the rest describe a manner of articulation that no single codepoint witnesses — so they are counted for paintability and inherit the oracle's verdict rather than testing it. Nothing here measures whether the COLOURS are right: the skin stays beta on a hafiz's sign-off (`plan-tajweed-golden-row`), and painting a wrong colour per word makes it wronger, not righter. Corrections 4–7 were found by looking at what the oracle got wrong, so overfitting is the standing risk; three things hold it in check and none is taste — each rule names a real orthographic feature and is applied to all 6,236 ayahs rather than the ayahs that motivated it, the oracle tests letter IDENTITY at a position the rule does not touch, and a rule that is too broad is punished immediately (generalising 4 costs 4.5 points). A rule that fixed only the ayah that suggested it was rejected for exactly that reason and 36:52 recorded as named instead. And the spans are measured against the PRINT's tokenisation, which is the question asked; PROVENANCE.md's 16.7% is against Tanzil's own, and the two numbers are not the same measurement even though they nearly agree.
